articles.title: Apple's iPhone Duo event should put the bears to rest
articles.summary: Apple, the innovator, just got its memory chip inflation-beating groove back.
articles.body:
I have heard this statement about Apple ( AAPL ) for three-plus years. Maybe you've heard it too.

I have heard all the bear arguments on Apple: That Apple doesn't have an answer to ChatGPT or Claude's answer engine. That Apple's Siri is a massive failure in AI. That the iPhone is simply a boring utility. That there's no autonomous electric Apple car driving. That OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) is testing new hardware designed by former Apple superhero Jony Ive.

But it's all rubbish that needs to be buried in the trash, at least for right now.

What Apple uncorked this week is a massive suite of innovation. So much so that you can't help but view the stock as a great buy at these valuation levels.

New Apple CEO John Ternus debuted the tech giant's first foldable iPhone this week, as we all know.

Dubbed the iPhone Duo, the device features a passport-like design that opens and closes like a book. It sports a 5.4-inch front display that expands to a massive 7.6-inch display when opened, ideal for watching movies, playing games, working, and multitasking.

The iPhone Duo will start at $1,999, in line with speculation ahead of Apple's annual event. The higher-spec Duo will cost north of $3,100.

Objectively, look at this phone and tell me it's not innovative. Tell me Android devices don't look like pure trash next to the Duo.

"Overall, key product feature announcements (debut of a foldable form factor model, Touch ID to open on the iPhone Duo, new A20-series chips, and rear-camera systems) were largely as expected, and should drive continued strength in device demand," Goldman Sachs analyst Michael Ng said.

Meanwhile, did you see that the new AirPods sport 50% more noise cancellation? Or the regular iPhone 18 Pro with supercharged battery life? How about the new Apple Watch that can summarize ambient conversations? (Creepy, yes, but innovative.)

I am not some wild-eyed tech blogger foaming at the mouth for every Apple product-reveal day. Just a consumer with an investing background who recognizes common sense when he sees it.

"Will iOS users view it differently, or will there be some unique take that Apple comes up with that changes that penetration dynamic a little bit?" AT&T CEO John Stankey told me at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia & Tech conference this week. "I suppose it's possible, but my guess right now is we're going to kind of see it contained to a portion of the user base that wants that larger device and is maybe willing to invest more money to pick it up and get it."

articles.title: Central Bank of AI: Analyst Says NVIDIA Could Sit on $1.4 Trillion — Dwarfing Hyperscalers and Wall Street
articles.summary: One analyst firm's five-year cash projection for NVIDIA would make the chip giant wealthier than every hyperscaler, every semiconductor rival, and most of th...
articles.body:
SemiAnalysis projects NVDA could accumulate $1.4 trillion in cash by fiscal 2031, with operating cash flow already surging to $103 billion annually.

NVIDIA mobilized $500 billion in third-party capital with Apollo, BlackRock, and KKR, positioning itself as both supplier and financier of the AI buildout.

Wall Street backs the compounding thesis with 57 buy ratings and a $328 price target, though export restrictions and margin compression remain key risks.

Research firm SemiAnalysis, in a September 11, 2026 note titled "Nvidia's Backstop Universe, Heads I Win, Tails Who Loses?", projects that NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) could accumulate roughly $1.4 trillion in cash and investments by fiscal 2031. That figure is an analyst projection rather than a reported balance-sheet number. It is grounded in consensus estimates of about $441 billion in EBITDA for fiscal 2028 alone, extrapolated across the remainder of the decade.

The projection is a compounding story built on NVIDIA's current cash engine. Fiscal year operating cash flow rose from $28.09 billion for the year ended January 31, 2024, to $64.09 billion for the year ended January 31, 2025, and then to $102.72 billion for the year ended January 31, 2026. The most recent quarter delivered $96.22 billion in revenue, up 105.8% year over year, with net income of $59.69 billion and non-GAAP gross margin of 75.0%.

24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now . Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.

And NVDA made the cut. See who else did.

The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.

The balance sheet already shows the shape of the argument. Total assets reached $320.27 billion as of July 31, 2026, with short-term investments of $76.93 billion and long-term investments of $51.16 billion layered on top of $22.44 billion in cash. Total debt sits at just $38.86 billion against $228.98 billion in shareholder equity. Management guided Q3 fiscal 2027 revenue to $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, and CFO Colette Kress told analysts NVIDIA expects fiscal 2028 revenue to grow approximately 70%.
